key_insight: ProtoDiffusion generates editable multi-layer images using one shared spatial prototype and one vector per layer, reducing latent token count from NHW to HW+N before backbone-specific packing.
engineering_relevance: This compact representation supports image- and text-conditioned design generation without requiring the layer count or layout as input, while accepting optional bounding-box guidance.
method: ProtoVAE encodes a design into a shared spatial prototype and per-layer candidate vectors.
A shared decoder reconstructs each RGBA layer conditioned on its candidate vector.
Latent diffusion jointly denoises the prototype and fixed candidate slots, leaving unused slots empty.
evidence_signal: ProtoVAE reaches 40.43 dB layer-crop PSNR; on LayerD, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 of 0.040 with boxes and 0.057 without, while text-to-design reaches merged-image FID of 66.41 versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein].
watch_item: Fixed candidate slots impose a configured layer-capacity limit, and token-count savings alone do not establish memory or runtime savings across backbones.
paper_title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
